item.text: I’m using the frontend-design skill to build a coffee-specific dashboard with a deep blue navigation rail, crisp lavender accents, and clear, practical data views. I’ll include working channel filters, sortable café columns, search, and mobile navigation in the single HTML file.

The design uses a navy-and-periwinkle palette, distinctive headings, and quiet tables so the morning priorities are easy to scan. I’ve kept the chart free of invented sparklines and added a stock alert for the two coffees under seven days. The revenue chart will also make clear that its supplied values are rounded to thousands.

/bin/zsh -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from collections import Counter
p=Path('index.html')
class Check(HTMLParser):
 def __init__(self): super().__init__(); self.ids=[]; self.refs=[]; self.remote_images=[]
 def handle_starttag(self,tag,attrs):
  a=dict(attrs)
  if 'id' in a:self.ids.append(a['id'])
  if tag=='use':self.refs.append(a.get('href','')[1:])
  if tag=='img' and a.get('src','').startswith('http'):self.remote_images.append(a['src'])
c=Check();c.feed(p.read_text())
assert not [k for k,n in Counter(c.ids).items() if n>1], 'Duplicate ids'
assert not set(c.refs)-set(c.ids), 'Missing SVG symbols'
assert not c.remote_images
assert [x.name for x in Path('.').iterdir() if x.is_file()]==['index.html']
print('HTML checks passed: unique IDs, resolved inline SVG icons, no remote images, one output file.')
print('File size:',p.stat().st_size,'bytes')
PY"
